AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 4, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

REGULAR MEETING
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:00 P.M.

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
   Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Bernie Araral
  New Harvest Christian Fellowship Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Natalie Rivera, 5th grade
  William Orr Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize Hometown Heroes.

  II.  City Council to recognize the winners of the “I Love Trees” Contest.

  III.  City Council to recognize Marie Olsen as Older American of the Year.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Memorial Day event recap.

  2.  Public Works Week event recap.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of April 30,
  May 7, 14, and 28, 2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the periods April 7, 2019 – April 20,
  2019, in the total amount of $903,998.98 and April 21, 2019 – May 4, 2019, in the total amount of
  $913,287.09. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant registers for the
  periods of May 1, 2019 – May 14, 2019, in the total amount of $1,647,739.09 and May 15, 2019 –
  May 29, 2019, in the total amount of $3,305,065.70. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY - Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Safeway
  Insurance (Hector Hernandez). 830-19
   Report

5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – MAY 22, 2019 - No action is required unless the City Council
  elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the Commission’s
  action was final. 320

  Synopsis

6.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-27 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS - Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 19-27, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE PUBLIC SAFETY
  DEPARTMENT. 870-02

  Report

7.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-29 – REVOCATION OF CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 934 AND ZONE
  VARIANCE NO. 333 - JAYNESHWAR GOUNDER, DHAKA LIQUOR AND MARKET, 10944 IMPERIAL
  HIGHWAY - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-29, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND
  DECISION RELATIVE TO THE REVOCATION OF ZONE VARIANCE NO. 333 AND CONDITIONAL
  USE PERMIT NO. 934. 320-01-934/320-11-333

  Report

8.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-30 – DENYING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1006 AND RESOLUTION
  NO. 19-31 – DENYING PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2001 – MALIK AHMAD, BEST RATE
  RECYCLING, LLC, 11018-11030 ROSECRANS AVENUE – A REQUEST TO: (1) ESTABLISH A
  RECYCLING CENTER WITHIN THE PARKING LOT OF AN EXISTING COMMERCIAL
  DEVELOPMENT AND OTHER SITE MODIFICATIONS AS REQUESTED – Staff recommends City
  Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 19-30, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION RELATIVE TO THE DENIAL OF
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1006; and

  b.  Resolution No. 19-31, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION RELATIVE TO THE DENIAL OF
  PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2001. 320-01-1006/320-04-2001

  Report

9.  2019 APPLICATIONS FOR RETAIL FIREWORKS SALES PERMITS - Staff recommends City Council
  approve the organizations eligible to obtain retail fireworks permits and authorize issuance of permits.
  612-08

  Report

10. AGREEMENT - CERTIFIED LEAD-BASED PAINT HAZARD EVALUATION, LEAD HAZARD
  ABATEMENT MONITORING, POST-ABATEMENT CLEARANCE TESTING, AND ASBESTOS
  TESTING – Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with Barr & Clark to provide
  certified lead-based paint hazard evaluation, lead hazard abatement monitoring, post-abatement
  clearance testing, and asbestos testing in the amount of $20,000 per year from July 1, 2019 to June
  30, 2024; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided
  there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 315-03

  Report

11. AGREEMENT - SERVICING HOME IMPROVEMENT LOANS – Staff recommends City Council
  approve an agreement with AmeriNational Community Services, LLC for loan services in the amount of
  $10,000 per year from July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2024; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 315-01-01
   Report

12. AGREEMENT - JOB TRAINING PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement
  with Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District for job training in the amount of $30,000 for the term of
  July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 315-01-02

  Report

13. AGREEMENT FOR FAIR HOUSING PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council approve an
  agreement with Fair Housing Foundation for a Fair Housing Program in the amount of $13,000 per
  year from July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2024; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement
  and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney. 315

  Report

14. PROJECT NO. 7521 – APPROVAL OF PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS AND AUTHORIZATION TO
  ADVERTISE FOR THE FISCAL YEAR (FY) 2017/18 SEWER SYSTEM REPAIR PROJECT - Staff
  recommends City Council approve the plans and specifications for the FY 2017/18 sewer system repair
  project, authorize the advertisement of bids, and set a bid opening date of June 26, 2019. 1005-04-
  7521

  Report

15. PROJECT NOS. 7441 AND 7519 - AWARD OF CONTRACT - PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING
  SERVICES FOR THE DESIGN OF A WATER AND SEWER SUPERVISORY CONTROL AND DATA
  ACQUISITION SYSTEM (SCADA) – Staff recommends City Council to award a contract to Cannon in
  the amount of $236,843 for the professional engineering services for the design of water and sewer
  SCADA system projects starting in July 2019 and ending March 2020; and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of
  the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7441/7519

  Report

16. AMENDMENT NO. 7 – WATER SYSTEM SERVICES – Staff recommends City Council approve
  Amendment No. 7 to the agreement with Bucknam and Associates to provide additional services and
  additional compensation in the amount of $15,000 for FY 2018/19; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the amendment, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1070-05

  Report

17. AGREEMENT – BUS CAPITAL TIRE LEASE PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council approve a
  lease agreement with The Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company for bus tire leasing for a three (3) year
  term from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022, with an option to extend the agreement for two (2) one-
  year periods for a total contract value of $281,713; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement, and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 634-03

  Report

18. AGREEMENT – AUTOMOTIVE PARTS AND SUPPLIES - Staff recommends City Council approve an
  agreement with Hanson Distributing Company for Automotive Parts and Supplies for a three (3) year
  term of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022 , with an option to extend the agreement for two (2) one-
  year periods for a total contract value of $200,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement, and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 634-05

  Report

19. AGREEMENT – NORWALK TRANSIT SYSTEM (NTS) BUS EXTERIOR ADVERTISING – Staff
  recommends City Council approve an agreement with Outfront Media, LLC for the NTS Advertising
  Program Services for a three (3) year term of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022, with an option to
  extend the agreement for two (2) one-year periods; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
   agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 1120-02

  Report

  20. AWARD CONTRACT FOR RODENT ABATEMENT SERVICES AT CITY PARKS AND FACILITIES
  FOR TURF AREAS – Staff recommends City Council award a contract to Animal Pest Management
  Services, Inc. in the amount of $26,964 for rodent abatement services at City parks and facilities for the
  term of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022; with the option to extend for two (2) additional one (1) year
  periods; and authorize the City Manager to execute the contract and any amendments provided there
  is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 920-03

  Report

  21. AWARD CONTRACT FOR POOL MAINTENANCE AND CHEMICAL SUPPLIES FOR LAP AND
  WADER POOLS AT THE NORWALK PARK AQUATIC PAVILION – Staff recommends City Council
  award a contract to The Illini Companies, Inc. DBA Commercial Aquatic Services in the amount of
  $30,780 to provide pool maintenance and chemical supplies for lap and wader pools at the Norwalk
  Park Aquatic Pavilion for the term of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022, with the option to extend for
  two (2) additional one (1) year periods; and authorize the City Manager to execute the contract and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 955

  Report

  22. RESOLUTION NO. 19-33 - AUTHORIZATION TO SUBMIT AN APPLICATION TO THE CALIFORNIA
  GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES FOR THE HAZARD MITIGATION GRANT
  PROGRAM AND DESIGNATING A CITY REPRESENTATIVE TO EXECUTE THE APPLICATION AND
  ANY ASSURANCES AND AGREEMENTS FOR ALL MATTERS PERTAINING TO SUCH STATE
  DISASTER ASSISTANCE FOR AND ON BEHALF OF THE CITY OF NORWALK – Staff recommends
  City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-33, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE SUBMITTAL OF AN APPLICATION TO THE CALIFORNIA
  GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES FOR THE HAZARD MITIGATION GRANT
  PROGRAM; AND DESIGNATING THE CITY MANAGER, DEPUTY CITY MANAGER, OR DIRECTOR
  OF PUBLIC SAFETY TO EXECUTE THE APPLICATION AND ANY ASSURANCES AND
  AGREEMENTS FOR ALL MATTERS PERTAINING TO SUCH STATE DISASTER ASSISTANCE FOR
  AND ON BEHALF OF THE CITY OF NORWALK.

  Report

  23. AGREEMENTS – HEALTH ON WHEELS PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  approve the Health on Wheels agreement with the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District and
  California State University Long Beach Foundation to provide free and accessible basic health
  care services to children in the NLMUSD from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022;

  b.  approve the Bailment agreement with Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District, for storage of a
  motor home vehicle at the Norwalk City Yard from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022; and

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute the HOW Program and Bailment agreements and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in forms approved by
  the City Attorney. 440

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  24. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING
   25. RESOLUTION NO. 19-32 - SETTING SEWER SERVICE CHARGE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 AND
  ORDERING THAT SUCH CHARGE BE COLLECTED ON THE TAX ROLL – Staff recommends City
  Council consider adopting Resolution No. 19-32, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING THE ANNUAL SEWER REPORT AND LEVYING AN ANNUAL
  SEWER SERVICE CHARGE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 PURSUANT TO CHAPTER 13.14 OF THE
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE AND ORDERING THE ANNUAL SEWER SERVICE CHARGE TO BE
  COLLECTED ON THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES TAX ROLL. 637

  Report

REPORTS

  26. AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE STAFF AUGMENTATION FOR THE DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC SERVICES
  AND AS NEEDED PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING PROJECT MANAGER SERVICES – Staff
  recommends City Council approve an agreement with Onward Engineering, to provide staff
  augmentation for the Director of Public Services and as needed Project Manager engineering services
  in an amount not to exceed $200,000 from July 1, 2019 through December 31, 2019, with an option to
  extend an additional six months; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 310-06

  Report

  27. AGREEMENT - HOMELESS SHELTER SERVICES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 – Staff recommends
  City Council approve an agreement with The Whole Child in the amount of $15,000 to provide
  homeless shelter services from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 425-03-16

  Report

  28. PROJECT NO. 3305-2069 - AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF
  LIGHT EMITTING DIODE (LED) FIXTURES FOR CITY-OWNED STREET LIGHT POLES,
  ENGINEERS REPORT NO. 19-11 – Staff recommends City Council award a contract to Siemens
  Mobility, Inc. of Austin, Texas in the amount of $1,416,465.51 for the purchase and installation of
  approximately 3,891 LED street light fixtures and related equipment; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1030

  Report

  29. PROJECT NO. 7440 - AWARD OF CONTRACTS FOR INSTALLATION OF WATER MAINS ON
  ALONDRA BOULEVARD, PIONEER BOULEVARD, AND 160TH STREET AND CONSTRUCTION
  MANAGEMENT OF THE PROJECT – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  award the construction contract to Williams Pipeline Contractor, in the amount of $783,070 for
  Project No. 7440, the Alondra Boulevard, Pioneer Boulevard, and 160th Street water main
  installation project;

  b.  award the construction management service contract to Civiltec Engineering, Inc., in the amount of
  $101,544.65; and

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreements and any amendments, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in forms approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7440

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated May 30, 2019.
 Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
